faults.title: Units available tile counts the catalogue as 40 units
faults.manifestation: The Units available tile on the desk overview reads "40" with the note "of 40 units in the catalogue". The note is supposed to state the catalogue's total unit count, which is 53, so the tile now claims the desk owns only the units that happen to be free.
faults.trigger_path: Open the desk overview at / and read the Units available tile and its note.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/overview — the request that carries the tile's numbers.

faults.title: Late business days counted from the day before the due date
faults.manifestation: The Overdue loans table on the desk overview says L-1042 is 4 business days late with a late fee today of $60.00. R8 counts the business days after the Wed 11 Mar due date up to the desk date — Thu 12, Fri 13 and Mon 16, three days — for a $45.00 fee on three units. The same inflated day count and fee follow through to the loan page's check-in notice and to the check-in banner.
faults.trigger_path: Open / and read the Business days late and Late fee today columns of the Overdue loans table, or open /loans/L-1042 and read the line above the check-in form.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/overview while the overdue list is non-empty, or GET /api/loans/:id for a loan that is overdue.

faults.title: Overdue card goes blank instead of showing its empty state
faults.manifestation: Once nothing is overdue — after the one overdue loan is checked in — the Overdue loans card on the desk overview is empty apart from its heading and its "Open in loans" link. The required empty state, heading "No overdue loans" with the body "Every loan that is out is still within its due date.", never appears.
faults.trigger_path: Check L-1042 in from /loans/L-1042 (any condition), then return to / and look at the Overdue loans card.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/overview whose overdue list is empty — the page render that should carry the empty state.
faults.check_note: Client-side rendering. Over HTTP the check proves the desk really has no overdue loans and that the served /views/overview.js has lost the empty-state call; the blank card itself wants one browser look.

faults.title: Late fees taken today never reach charges booked today
faults.manifestation: Checking the overdue loan L-1042 in charges a $45.00 late fee and says so in the banner, but the desk overview's Charges booked today tile stays at $341.00 instead of moving to $386.00. A fee charged at the desk today is silently missing from the day's takings.
faults.trigger_path: Read Charges booked today on /, check L-1042 in with condition Good from /loans/L-1042, then return to / and read the tile again.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/overview once a loan has been checked in today with a late fee above zero.

faults.title: Empty catalogue result never quotes the search term
faults.manifestation: A catalogue search that matches nothing shows "No equipment matches these filters" with the body "No catalogue item matches the filters you picked.", even though a search term is sitting in the Search equipment box and in the URL. The required body "Nothing in the catalogue matches “<search text>”." never appears.
faults.trigger_path: Open /equipment, type a term that matches nothing (for example "zeppelin") into Search equipment, and press Apply filters.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/equipment carrying a non-empty q whose result is empty — the request behind the empty state.
faults.check_note: Client-side rendering. Over HTTP the check proves the search really matched nothing and that the served /views/equipment-list.js no longer holds the searched-for wording; the rendered body wants one browser look.

faults.title: Unknown catalogue item is refused with the loans sentence
faults.manifestation: Opening an equipment address that does not exist shows the "Something went wrong" page with the error banner "That loan does not exist." The address is an equipment item, and the required sentence is "That equipment item does not exist."
faults.trigger_path: Open /equipment/no-such-item (or follow any broken equipment link) and read the error banner.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/equipment/:id that answers 404.

faults.title: Available now only filters nothing
faults.manifestation: Ticking "Available now only" and pressing Apply filters changes nothing: all 12 items stay listed, "Showing 12 of 12 equipment items." is unchanged, and the DJI RS 4 Pro Gimbal is still there with its "Fully booked" pill — while the checkbox stays ticked and the URL carries availableOnly=1. The desk overview's Units available tile leads to the same unfiltered list.
faults.trigger_path: Open /equipment, tick Available now only, press Apply filters; or click the Units available tile on /.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/equipment carrying an availableOnly query parameter.

faults.title: The Out status filter hides overdue loans
faults.manifestation: Filtering the loans list by status Out lists 2 loans and says "Showing 2 of 8 loans.", leaving out the overdue loan L-1042 even though its status is out. The desk overview's Out on loan tile says 3 and links straight to this list.
faults.trigger_path: Open /loans, choose Status "Out", press Apply filters; or click the Out on loan tile on /.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/loans with status=out.

faults.title: Cancel loan is offered nowhere
faults.manifestation: No loan offers a Cancel loan button any more. L-1043, waiting on the pickup shelf, shows only Mark picked up, and the two awaiting-approval requests show only Go to approvals, so a booking can never be withdrawn and its units never go back into stock before pickup.
faults.trigger_path: Open /loans/L-1043 or /loans/L-1044 and look at the action panel for Cancel loan.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/loans/:id for a loan whose status is pending_approval or ready — the page render that should carry the button.

faults.title: Yes, cancel loan does nothing
faults.manifestation: Cancel loan opens the confirmation reading "Cancel L-1043? Its 2 units go back into stock straight away.", but pressing "Yes, cancel loan" does nothing at all: no banner, no change of status, and the loan is still ready for pickup after a reload. Only "Keep loan" has any effect.
faults.trigger_path: Open /loans/L-1043, press Cancel loan, then press Yes, cancel loan. Reachable only once f-cancel-button-missing is withdrawn, since the button is otherwise absent.
faults.probe_note: The click sends no request, so the probe is the nearest server-observable signal: GET /api/loans/:id for a cancellable loan — the page render that carries the confirmation block.
faults.check_note: Client-side handler. Over HTTP the check proves the loan is cancellable and that the served /views/loan-detail.js no longer posts the cancellation; the dead button wants one browser look.

faults.title: The Extension block is gone from an out loan
faults.manifestation: The "Out with the borrower" panel on an out loan has lost its whole Extension section: no "Extension" heading, no "One extension is allowed. It would move the due date to …" line and no "Extend by 7 days" button. Only the Check in form is left, so a loan can never be extended.
faults.trigger_path: Open /loans/L-1048 (out, not overdue, never extended) and look for the Extension block above Check in.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/loans/:id for a loan whose status is out — the page render that should carry the block.
faults.check_note: Client-side rendering. Over HTTP the check proves the loan is out and extendable and that the served /views/loan-detail.js no longer renders the block; the missing section wants one browser look.

faults.title: A loan can be extended more than once
faults.manifestation: After L-1048 has been extended once, its Schedule panel says "One 7-day extension used" while the Extension block still says "One extension is allowed." with an enabled Extend by 7 days button. Pressing it again is accepted and pushes the due date another seven days, instead of refusing with "This loan has already used its one extension."
faults.trigger_path: Open /loans/L-1048, press Extend by 7 days, then press it again on the reloaded page. Reachable only once f-extension-block-missing is withdrawn.
faults.probe_note: POST /api/loans/:id/extend on a loan that has already used an extension, whether it is accepted or refused.

faults.title: Three units miss the bundle discount
faults.manifestation: A loan of exactly three units earns no bundle discount: step 3 shows no "Bundle discount (3+ units)" line and a total 10% too high — three GoPro Hero 12 kits for 7 days come to $126.00 instead of $113.40. Four or more units still discount correctly, and the seeded three-unit loan L-1042 keeps its stored $23.10 discount.
faults.trigger_path: New loan → step 1 → step 2: add 3 units of one item (GoPro Hero 12 ×3), loan period 7 days → Continue to review, and read the Charges panel.
faults.probe_note: A draft request (GET or PATCH /api/loan-drafts/:id) whose lines total exactly 3 units, or a submitted 3-unit loan.

faults.title: A Saturday due date rolls forward only one day
faults.manifestation: A due date that lands on a Saturday is moved forward one day to the Sunday instead of two days to the Monday, so the desk promises a return on a day it is closed. Booking a 1-day loan for pickup Fri 20 Mar 2026 shows Due back "Sun 22 Mar 2026, 17:00" on step 3 and on the booked loan; R3 makes it Mon 23 Mar 2026. Extensions that land on a Saturday move the same wrong way.
faults.trigger_path: New loan → step 2: any item, loan period 1 day, pickup date 2026-03-20 → Continue to review and read Due back.
faults.probe_note: A draft, booking or extension whose pickup date plus loan period (or due date plus seven days) lands on a weekend.

faults.title: A refused booking gives no feedback at all
faults.manifestation: When confirming is refused because another loan took the last free units while the draft sat on step 3, the page says nothing: Confirm booking runs its 0.9 second "Booking…" spell, comes back enabled, and step 3 sits there unchanged with no error banner. No loan is created and the supervisor is given no reason.
faults.trigger_path: Take two drafts to step 3 for the last free unit of the same item (Canon C70 has one unit free), confirm the first draft, then confirm the second.
faults.probe_note: POST /api/loan-drafts/:id/submit that answers 4xx — the refusal the page should have shown.
faults.check_note: Client-side handler. Over HTTP the check drives the real conflict, proves the desk returned the availability refusal, and proves the served /views/new-loan.js no longer renders it; the silent page wants one browser look.

faults.title: A confirmed booking strands the flow on step 3
faults.manifestation: Confirming a booking creates the loan but leaves the browser on step 3: no success banner such as "L-1049 booked and ready for pickup on Tue 17 Mar 2026." and no move to the new loan's page. Pressing Confirm booking again then reports "That draft loan has expired. Start a new loan.", so the supervisor cannot tell whether the loan was booked.
faults.trigger_path: New loan → step 2 → step 3 → Confirm booking, and watch where the page lands.
faults.probe_note: POST /api/loan-drafts/:id/submit that answers 201.
faults.check_note: Client-side navigation. Over HTTP the check proves the loan really was created with its success message and that the served /views/new-loan.js no longer sets the banner or navigates; the stranded page wants one browser look.

faults.title: Step 2 item rows have no Remove button
faults.manifestation: Every item row on step 2 of the new-loan flow has an empty Action column: the Remove button is gone, so an item added by mistake cannot be taken off the draft. The only way out is to abandon the draft and start again.
faults.trigger_path: New loan → step 2 → pick an item and press Add item → look at the Action column of the new row.
faults.probe_note: GET or PATCH /api/loan-drafts/:id for a draft that already holds at least one item — the step-2 render that should carry the buttons.
faults.check_note: Client-side rendering. Over HTTP the check proves the draft holds an item row and that the served /views/new-loan.js no longer builds a Remove button; the empty Action column wants one browser look.

faults.title: A running approval says Declining…
faults.manifestation: Pressing Approve disables the button and relabels it "Declining…" for the 0.6 seconds the decision takes, while the status line beside it reads "Recording your approval…". The request is then approved with "L-1044 approved and moved to ready for pickup.", so the button contradicts both the line beside it and the outcome.
faults.trigger_path: Open /approvals and press Approve on a request; watch the button label while it runs.
faults.probe_note: POST /api/approvals/:id/approve that answers 200 — the 0.6 second window the label is shown for.
faults.check_note: Client-side, and visible only while the action runs. Over HTTP the check proves the approval works and that the served /views/approvals.js no longer carries the "Approving…" label; the transient label wants one browser look.

faults.title: A running decline shows no status line
faults.manifestation: Confirming a decline disables the button and shows "Declining…", but the status line "Recording your decision…" that should appear beside it never does. For the 0.6 seconds the decision takes the queue gives no running feedback other than the button.
faults.trigger_path: Open /approvals, press Decline, type a reason, press Confirm decline, and watch for the status line beside the button.
faults.probe_note: POST /api/approvals/:id/decline that answers 200 — the 0.6 second window the line is shown for.
faults.check_note: Client-side, and visible only while the action runs. Over HTTP the check proves the decline works and that the served /views/approvals.js no longer passes the status host for the decline; the missing line wants one browser look.

faults.title: The emptied approvals queue offers no way onward
faults.manifestation: Once every request has been decided the approvals queue shows "Nothing waiting for approval" and its explanatory line, but the "View all loans" button that should sit beneath it is absent, leaving the page a dead end.
faults.trigger_path: Approve L-1044 and decline L-1045 (or cancel both), then look at /approvals.
faults.probe_note: GET /api/approvals whose count is zero — the render that should carry the button.
faults.check_note: Client-side rendering. Over HTTP the check proves the queue really is empty and that the served /views/approvals.js no longer builds the button; the dead-end empty state wants one browser look.
